def-ip-distributions-conormal-kernels-an:
## Definition

Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold. A distribution on $M$ is a continuous complex-linear functional on compactly supported smooth densities on $M$. Its topology is generated locally by the fixed-support seminorms $\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\sup_K|\partial^\alpha\varphi|$, followed by the locally convex test-function topology. In a chart $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ a test density is $\varphi(x)|dx|$; under a coordinate change it transforms by the absolute Jacobian. A distribution is compactly supported when its support, the complement of its largest vanishing open set, is compact.

For a smooth submersion $p:Y\to M$, define the pullback $p^*u$ by transposing fiber integration: in submersion coordinates $p(x,v)=x$,
$$
\langle p^*u,\psi(x,v)|dx\,dv|\rangle =\left\langle u,\left(\int\psi(x,v)|dv|\right)|dx|\right\rangle.
$$
The absolute density quotient gives the fiber density in other submersion coordinates. For a distributional density $V$ on $Y$, meaning a continuous functional on compactly supported smooth scalar functions, define its support by the same largest-vanishing-open-set rule. If $q:Y\to M$ is proper on $\operatorname{supp}V$, then for a test function $\varphi$ on $M$ the set $q^{-1}(\operatorname{supp}\varphi)\cap\operatorname{supp}V$ is compact. Choose a smooth compact cutoff $\beta$ equal to one near this set and define the pushforward by
$$
\langle q_*V,\varphi\rangle=\langle V,\beta(\varphi\circ q)\rangle.
$$
The support property makes this independent of $\beta$; the cutoff is needed because $\varphi\circ q$ need not be compactly supported on all of $Y$.
A smooth density $\mu$ times a distribution $u$ in the test-density convention is the distributional density $\mu u$ defined by $\langle\mu u,\varphi\rangle=\langle u,\varphi\mu\rangle$.

Let $Z\subseteq G\times X$ be an embedded submanifold whose two projections are submersions. For a smooth density $\omega_Z$ on $Z$, its incidence delta kernel is the distributional density
$$
\langle K_Z,\Phi\rangle=\int_Z\Phi|_Z\,\omega_Z.
$$
In coordinates $(g,x)=(u,t)$ with $Z=\{t=0\}$, this is the delta distribution in the $t$ variables paired with the chosen density on $Z$. The conormal bundle and associated cotangent relation are
$$
N^*Z=\{(z,\zeta)\in T^*(G\times X):z\in Z,\ \zeta|_{T_zZ}=0\}, \qquad C_Z=\{(g,\eta;x,\xi):(g,x;\eta,-\xi)\in N^*Z\setminus0\}.
$$
Here $N^*Z\setminus0$ removes the zero covector, and the minus sign is the distribution-kernel convention for an operator from $X$ to $G$. Since both projections are submersions, every nonzero conormal in this relation has both $\eta\ne0$ and $\xi\ne0$. An analytic incidence kernel means that $Z$, its local defining maps, and the coefficients of $\omega_Z$ are real analytic. This definition covers the incidence kernels used below; it does not assert a general Fourier-integral-operator calculus.
lem-ip-analytic-cutoff-sequence:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subset\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $K\subset U$ be compact. There are constants $A,C>0$ and functions $\chi_N\in C_c^\infty(U)$ for each integer $N\ge1$ such that $0\le\chi_N\le1$, $\chi_N=1$ on a fixed neighborhood of $K$, and
$$
|\partial^\alpha\chi_N(x)|\le C(AN)^{|\alpha|} \qquad (x\in\mathbb R^n,\ |\alpha|\le N).
$$
These are smooth compact cutoffs; no compactly supported analytic function is asserted.
lem-ip-holomorphic-morse-normalization-a:
## Statement

Let $\phi$ be holomorphic on a neighborhood of $0\in\mathbb C^n$, with $d\phi(0)=0$ and complex Hessian $H=\phi''(0)$ invertible. There is a local biholomorphic coordinate map $w=\Psi(z)$ with $\Psi(0)=0$ such that
$$
\phi(z)=\phi(0)+\tfrac12\sum_{j=1}^n w_j^2.
$$
Its linear part satisfies $(\det D\Psi(0))^2=\det H$. For a continuous parameter family of invertible Hessians $H(p)$, near any fixed parameter $p_0$ the determinant remains in a disc avoiding $0$; choosing one square root at $p_0$ therefore fixes a continuous branch on that neighborhood. If $\operatorname{Re}H$ is positive definite, then
$$
\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{-\lambda x^THx/2}\,dx =(2\pi/\lambda)^{n/2}(\det H)^{-1/2},\qquad \lambda>0,
$$
with the integral interpreted as an absolutely convergent improper integral and the branch analytically continued from real positive-definite matrices. Finally, deforming a holomorphic contour preserves the integral of a holomorphic top-degree form when the contours are homologous through a region of holomorphy and the swept boundary integrals tend to zero.
def-ip-analytic-double-fibration-transfo:
## Definition

An analytic double fibration is a diagram of real-analytic manifolds and real-analytic submersions
$$
G\xleftarrow{\ \pi_G\ }Z\xrightarrow{\ \pi_X\ }X
$$
such that $Z$ is embedded in $G\times X$, both projections are submersions, and
$$
\dim G+\dim X>\dim Z>\dim G\ge\dim X.
$$
Write $C_Z=\{(g,\eta;x,\xi):(g,x;\eta,-\xi)\in N^*Z\setminus0\}$ for the incidence cotangent relation. Assume $\pi_G$ is proper on $\pi_X^{-1}(K)$ for every compact $K\subset X$. Let $\omega_Z$ be a nowhere vanishing real-analytic smooth density on $Z$ and let $\kappa\colon Z\to\mathbb C$ be real analytic and nowhere zero. For a compactly supported distribution $u$ on $X$, the weighted transform is the distributional density
$$
Ru=(\pi_G)_*\bigl(\kappa\,\omega_Z\,\pi_X^*u\bigr),
$$
where pullback, multiplication by a density, proper pushforward, and $C_Z$ use the conventions of the preceding definition. In local fiber coordinates this is integration of $u$ over the incidence fibers with weight $\kappa$ and density $\omega_Z$. The hypotheses on proper support ensure this transform is defined for every compactly supported input. This is the class treated on this page; no noisy-data or stability assertion is included.
def-ip-analytic-wavefront-fbi-transform:
## Definition

Let $u$ be a distribution, not necessarily compactly supported, or a distributional density (a continuous functional on compactly supported smooth scalar functions), on a real-analytic $n$-manifold $X$. Let $x_0$ lie in an analytic coordinate chart and let $\xi_0\in T^*_{x_0}X\setminus\{0\}$ have coordinate components in that chart. For $\chi\in C_c^\infty$ supported in the chart and equal to $1$ near $x_0$, define the Gaussian FBI packet
$$
\mathcal F_\chi u(x,\lambda\omega) =\left\langle u(y),\chi(y) \exp\!\left(i\lambda(x-y)\cdot\omega-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}|x-y|^2\right)\right\rangle, \quad \lambda\ge1,\quad |\omega|=1.
$$
When $u$ is a scalar distribution, the pairing is with the displayed function times coordinate density $|dy|$; when $u$ is a distributional density, the pairing is with the displayed scalar function. In both cases $\lambda\omega$ is the cotangent frequency. The covector $(x_0,\xi_0)$ is analytically regular for $u$ in this chart if there are such a cutoff $\chi$, a neighborhood $U$ of $x_0$, an open neighborhood $\Gamma$ of $\xi_0/|\xi_0|$ in the unit sphere, and constants $c,C>0$ such that
$$
|\mathcal F_\chi u(x,\lambda\omega)|\le C e^{-c\lambda} \quad(x\in U,\ \omega\in\Gamma,\ \lambda\ge1).
$$
The analytic wavefront set $\operatorname{WF}_A(u)$ is the set of nonzero cotangent vectors for which this exponential estimate fails. This is a chart-local definition. The separate local FBI-invariance claim needed for a geometric interpretation is stated by the companion lemma.
thm-ip-analytic-stationary-phase-with-ex:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded open set, let $\Phi$ be holomorphic on a complex neighborhood of $\overline U$, and let $a\in C_c^\infty(U)$ have a holomorphic extension near $0$. Assume $0\in\operatorname{supp}a$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi_0$, $d\Phi(0)=0$, and $d\Phi(x)\ne0$ at every $x\in\operatorname{supp}a\setminus\{0\}$. Let $H=-i\Phi''(0)$ be complex symmetric with positive-definite real part. Assume there are $r,c_0,d_0>0$ such that
$$
\operatorname{Im}(\Phi(x)-\Phi_0)\ge c_0|x|^2 \quad(|x|\le r),\qquad \operatorname{Im}(\Phi(x)-\Phi_0)\ge d_0 \quad(x\in\operatorname{supp}a,\ |x|\ge r).
$$
Let $\chi_N$ be the finite-order cutoff sequence equal to one on a fixed neighborhood of $0$, with $0\le\chi_N\le1$, and supported where these phase hypotheses hold. For every integer $N\ge1$ and every $\lambda\ge1$, put $I_N(\lambda)=\int e^{i\lambda\Phi(x)}a(x)\chi_N(x)\,dx$. There are coefficients $c_j$ determined by the full Taylor series of the phase and amplitude at $0$ and constants $C,\delta>0$, independent of $N,\lambda$, such that
$$
I_N(\lambda)=e^{i\lambda\Phi_0}(2\pi/\lambda)^{n/2}(\det H)^{-1/2} \left(\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}c_j\lambda^{-j}\right)+E_N(\lambda),
$$
$$
|c_j|\le C^{j+1}j!,\qquad |e^{-i\lambda\Phi_0}E_N(\lambda)|\le C^{N+1}N!\lambda^{-N-n/2}+Ce^{-\delta\lambda}.
$$
The square-root branch is fixed by the preceding holomorphic Morse/Gaussian-contour lemma, and $c_0=a(0)$. Taking $N=\lfloor\epsilon\lambda\rfloor$ for sufficiently small fixed $\epsilon>0$ and sufficiently large $\lambda$ makes the normalized remainder $e^{-i\lambda\Phi_0}E_N(\lambda)=O(e^{-\delta_2\lambda})$ for some $\delta_2>0$. The expansion includes every coefficient through the stated truncation order; it is not only a leading-term estimate.
def-ip-bolker-condition:
## Definition

For an analytic double fibration with incidence cotangent relation $C_Z\subset(T^*G\setminus0)\times(T^*X\setminus0)$, let
$$
\pi_L:C_Z\longrightarrow T^*G\setminus0,\qquad \pi_L(g,\eta;x,\xi)=(g,\eta).
$$
The double fibration satisfies the global Bolker condition if $\pi_L$ is an injective immersion. The Bolker condition holds at a specified point $c=(g,\eta;x,\xi)\in C_Z$ if the full fiber over its data covector is the singleton $\pi_L^{-1}(g,\eta)=\{c\}$ and $d\pi_L|_c$ is injective. Thus the pointwise condition has both a fiber-uniqueness clause, which excludes every other relation point over the same data covector even outside a chosen chart, and a local differential-rank clause.
lem-ip-double-fibration-conormal-kernel:
## Statement

Let $Z\subseteq G\times X$ be an embedded incidence submanifold of codimension $k>0$, and let $(g_0,x_0)\in Z$. Choose coordinates near this point and a submersion $F:G\times X\to\mathbb R^k$ with $Z=\{F=0\}$. Write $F=(F_1,\ldots,F_k)$. For every $\tau\in\mathbb R^k\setminus\{0\}$, the conormal covector at $(g,x)\in Z$ is
$$
(g,x;D_gF(g,x)^T\tau,\ D_xF(g,x)^T\tau).
$$
Consequently the incidence kernel has local delta representation $b(g,x)\delta(F(g,x))|dg\,dx|$, with a smooth density coefficient $b$, and its cotangent relation consists exactly of
$$
(g,D_gF^T\tau;\ x,-D_xF^T\tau),\qquad (g,x)\in Z,\quad \tau\ne0.
$$
No general Fourier-integral-operator composition calculus is used.
lem-ip-local-analytic-elliptic-packet-ca:
## Statement

Work near $(q_0,p_0)\in\mathbb R^n\times(\mathbb R^n\setminus0)$. A normalized positive analytic packet phase is a holomorphic function $\phi(y,q,p)$ on a fixed complex neighborhood of the indicated real variables, such that, for real arguments,
$$
\phi(q,q,p)=0,\qquad \partial_y\phi(q,q,p)=-p,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\phi(y,q,p)\ge c|y-q|^2
$$
for some $c>0$. A classical analytic amplitude is realized on each smaller complex neighborhood by
$$
a(y,q,p;\lambda)=\sum_{j<\epsilon\lambda}a_j(y,q,p)\lambda^{-j},\qquad \sup|a_j|\le C^{j+1}j!,
$$
with sufficiently small fixed $\epsilon>0$. Changing $\epsilon$ to a smaller positive number changes the realization by an exponentially small function on a smaller neighborhood. An elliptic amplitude has $a_0(q_0,q_0,p_0)\ne0$.

For a distribution $u$ localized to a sufficiently small fixed compact neighborhood of $q_0$, the uniform exponential decay of
$$
\langle u(y),a(y,q,p;\lambda)e^{i\lambda\phi(y,q,p)}\rangle
$$
for $(q,p)$ in a neighborhood of $(q_0,p_0)$ is independent of the normalized positive phase and elliptic classical analytic amplitude. Smooth fixed cutoffs equal to one near the packet centers are understood. This criterion agrees with the Gaussian criterion with unit directions and arbitrary $\lambda\ge1$.

More precisely, after shrinking the parameter neighborhood $W$, every other such packet $v_\beta$ with $\beta$ in a smaller $W_0\Subset W$ has a representation
$$
v_\beta(y;\lambda)=\int_W a(y,\alpha;\lambda)e^{i\lambda\phi(y,\alpha)}K(\beta,\alpha;\lambda)\,d\alpha+R_\beta(y;\lambda),
$$
where $|K|\le C\lambda^L$ and $\|R_\beta\|_{C^m}\le C_m e^{-c_m\lambda}$ on the fixed localization compact, for every fixed $m$. There is a representation in the reverse direction as well. All estimates are uniform on the stated smaller neighborhoods. Thus the inverse is an actual local operator modulo exponentially small errors, rather than just a formal inverse series.
lem-ip-analytic-nonstationary-incidence-:
## Statement

Let $R$ be an analytic double-fibration transform and $u\in\mathcal E'(X)$ with support $K$. Fix a nonzero data covector $(z_0,\zeta_0)$. Suppose there is no relation point $(z_0,\zeta_0;x,\xi)\in C_Z$ with $x\in K$. Then $(z_0,\zeta_0)\notin\operatorname{WF}_A(Ru)$. More precisely, the transpose of a data Gaussian packet, localized near $z_0$, is exponentially small with every fixed number of object derivatives on a neighborhood of $K$, uniformly for data centers and directions near $(z_0,\zeta_0/|\zeta_0|)$.
lem-ip-analytic-cutoff-sequence-and-fbi-:
## Statement

Let $u$ be a compactly supported distribution or a compactly supported distributional density on a real-analytic manifold. In each analytic chart use the Gaussian FBI packets of the preceding definition, paired with test densities in the first case and test functions in the second. The exponential-decay criterion is independent of the compact cutoff that equals one near the base point. It is also equivalent after an analytic chart change, with covectors transformed by the cotangent differential, and after replacing the standard Gaussian packets by their analytic pullbacks under that chart change. The latter equivalence is asserted only for the local packet and chart changes used on this page; it is the analytic-wavefront invariance needed to interpret the set geometrically.
lem-ip-bolker-geometric-criteria:
## Statement

Let $Z\subset G\times X$ be an analytic double fibration, and fix a local parameterization of its fibers over $G$,
$$
(g,s)\longmapsto (g,x(g,s)),
$$
where $s\in\mathbb R^d$ and $D_sx$ has rank $d$. Define
$$
E_g=\{(s,\xi):\xi\in T^*_{x(g,s)}X\setminus0,\ (D_sx(g,s))^T\xi=0\}, \qquad L_g(s,\xi)=(D_gx(g,s))^T\xi.
$$
On the cotangent relation over this incidence chart, the left projection is
$$
(g,s,\xi)\longmapsto(g,L_g(s,\xi)).
$$
Consequently it is injective on this chart portion exactly when each map $(s,\xi)\mapsto L_g(s,\xi)$ is injective on $E_g$. Its differential is injective exactly when the only $(\dot s,\dot\xi)$ satisfying
$$
(D_sx)^T\dot\xi+(D_s^2x[\dot s,\cdot])^T\xi=0,\qquad (D_sD_gx[\dot s,\cdot])^T\xi+(D_gx)^T\dot\xi=0
$$
is $(0,0)$. At a specified point of the full relation, the Bolker condition also requires that no point outside this chart portion has the same data covector; this is the global fiber-singleton clause. The displayed system is the local differential rank test.
lem-ip-flat-one-sided-analytic-support:
## Statement

Let $u$ be a distribution near $0\in\mathbb R^n$, vanishing where $x_n<0$. If either $(0,dx_n)$ or $(0,-dx_n)$ is absent from its Gaussian analytic wavefront set, then $u=0$ on a neighborhood of $0$. Equivalently, if $0\in\operatorname{supp}u$, both normal orientations belong to that wavefront set. The assertion also holds with the two half-spaces interchanged.
lem-ip-local-bolker-positive-packet-esti:
## Statement

Let $R$ be an analytic double-fibration transform, and fix a relation point $(z_0,\zeta_0;x_0,\xi_0)$ at which $d\pi_L$ is injective. For distributions $u$ supported in a sufficiently small neighborhood of $x_0$, data Gaussian exponential regularity at $(z_0,\zeta_0)$ implies object Gaussian exponential regularity at $(x_0,\xi_0)$.

More precisely, for data parameters $v=(q,p)$ near that point on the local embedded image $V$ of $\pi_L$, write $\chi(v)=(X(v),\Xi(v))$ for the paired object covector. The transpose localized data Gaussian has the form
$$
K_\lambda(x,v)=\lambda^{-d/2}e^{i\lambda\psi(x,v)}A(x,v;\lambda)+E_\lambda(x,v), \qquad d=\dim Z-\dim X,
$$
where $A$ is an elliptic classical analytic amplitude, $E_\lambda=O(e^{-c_m\lambda})$ in every fixed object derivative, and
$$
\psi(X(v),v)=-q\cdot p,\quad d_x\psi(X(v),v)=-\Xi(v),\quad \operatorname{Im}\psi(x,v)\ge c|x-X(v)|^2
$$
for real parameters. The map $\chi$ is an analytic submersion onto an open object cotangent neighborhood and has a local analytic section there. The constant factor in the kernel formula includes the nonzero Gaussian determinant on its continuous branch.
lem-ip-one-sided-analytic-support-contin:
## Statement

Let $X$ be a real-analytic manifold, let $x_0\in X$, and let $\Sigma$ be a $C^2$ hypersurface through $x_0$, meaning that in a smooth local chart it is the graph of a $C^2$ function with nonzero conormal $
u_0\in T^*_{x_0}X$. Let $f\in\mathcal D'(X)$ vanish on one side of $\Sigma$ in a neighborhood of $x_0$, meaning that in such a chart its restriction is zero on either the strict epigraph or strict subgraph of that defining function. If either $(x_0,
u_0)
otin\operatorname{WF}_A(f)$ or $(x_0,-
u_0)
otin\operatorname{WF}_A(f)$, then $f=0$ in a neighborhood of $x_0$.
thm-ip-analytic-wavefront-recovery-under:
## Statement

Let $R$ be an analytic double-fibration transform and let
$$
(z_0,\zeta_0;x_0,\xi_0)\in C_Z
$$
be a point of its incidence cotangent relation. Assume the Bolker condition holds at this point, meaning $\pi_L^{-1}(z_0,\zeta_0)=\{(z_0,\zeta_0;x_0,\xi_0)\}$ and $d\pi_L$ is injective at that relation point. For every compactly supported distribution $f\in\mathcal E'(X)$, if $(z_0,\zeta_0)\notin\operatorname{WF}_A(Rf)$, then $(x_0,\xi_0)\notin\operatorname{WF}_A(f)$. This is a qualitative microlocal implication; it asserts no noisy-data stability estimate.
thm-ip-local-support-from-one-sided-vani:
## Statement

Let $R$ be an analytic double-fibration transform, let $(z_0,\zeta_0;x_0,\eta_0)\in C_Z$, and let $\Sigma$ be a $C^2$ hypersurface through $x_0$ with $(x_0,\eta_0)\in N^*\Sigma\setminus0$. Let $f\in\mathcal E'(X)$ vanish on one side of $\Sigma$ near $x_0$. If the pointwise Bolker condition holds at $(z_0,\zeta_0;x_0,\eta_0)$ and $Rf=0$ in a neighborhood of $z_0$, then $f=0$ in a neighborhood of $x_0$.
